**Verdict:** moderately worried about breakage, seriously worried about the 80% concentration. They are 2 different risks w/ different fixes.

**Risk 1: DOM breakage (will happen, recoverable)**
YouTube ships DOM changes & A/B experiments constantly, so expect several breaks/yr. Cost = signups lost × time to fix, so cut time to fix:
- **Remote selector config:** serve selectors as JSON from your server, so a fix ships in min w/o Chrome Web Store review (hrs to days). MV3 bans remote code, not remote data.
- **Stable anchors:** prefer the `<video>` element, element IDs, `ytd-*` custom tags, aria attributes & URL patterns over class names or nth-child chains. Use 2-3 fallback selectors per target.
- **Canary:** Playwright w/ the extension loaded against live YouTube, hourly, logged-in & logged-out, page on failure.
- **Client telemetry:** report selector-miss rate per version. YouTube rolls out gradually, so a rise from 0 to 5% warns you before full rollout.
- **Graceful degradation:** on a miss, fall back to a UI you control (popup, side panel, floating button), never a silent no-op.
- **Official APIs:** move whatever you can to the Data API or IFrame Player API.

**Risk 2: platform (rare, potentially terminal)**
- **Store takedown or policy change:** audit against Chrome Web Store policies (single purpose, data disclosure, minimal permissions). Much higher risk if you touch ads, downloads or scraping.
- **YouTube ships your feature natively or blocks you:** no technical fix, only diversification.

**Concentration (the real fix)**
- **Own the user:** capture email or account at install, so a dead extension costs new signups, not the existing base.
- **Port:** Firefox, Edge & Safari are cheap and hedge against a Chrome-only takedown.
- **2nd channel:** build one now (SEO, web app, integrations, referral) and set a target, e.g. extension <50% of new users in 12 months.

**Order**
1. Telemetry + canary (days).
2. Remote config + fallback UI (1-2 wks).
3. Email capture at install.
4. Policy audit.
5. 2nd channel (ongoing).
